To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the application of thin nonlinear grading material on insulator structures can be simulated using the 2D FEM approach and the results can be used for further investigations.
the application of a thin mu-varistors layer can be a good alternative to the traditional grading rings in order to avoid the flashover on composite insulator structure under the polluted condition.
the use of nonlinear materials on composite insulators is a good solution for reducing the leakage current and the electric field strength on the insulators surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrostatic and electro- quasistatic simulation of insulators with nonlinear materials and thin resistive pollution layers.
the electrostatics of high-voltage insulators.
the development of a new method for the simulation of electro-quasistatic high voltage field problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the simulation model with thin resistive layer is a good approximation of a real insulator with a thin resistive layer.
the simulation results are in very good agreement with the experimental measurements.
the application of thin mu-varistor layers to the insulator structure has a positive effect in terms of the electric field distribution and the electric field strength in the insulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FEM simulation of high voltage insulator systems with resistive layers is possible with a 2D surface model.
we can use the FEM simulations for the design of high voltage insulators covered with thin resistive pollution layers.
the simulation results show a good agreement with measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thin resistive layer is able to reduce the surface electric field strength on the insulator surface.
thin resistive layers can be used as a cost-effective alternative to the nonlinear field grading material in composite insulators.
the use of nonlinear grading materials can reduce the electric field at the insulator surface.
